title: Numbers
summary: Numeric values: integers like 42 and decimals like 3.5. Luau stores them as double-precision floats by default, with `//` floor division and the math library for everything else.

details.heading: Representation
details.body: By default all numbers are 64-bit doubles (precise for integers up to 2^53). Luau also has an optional 32-bit integer mode for specialized use.

details.heading: Operators
details.body: `+ - * /` arithmetic, `//` floor division, `^` power (returns float), `%` modulo, unary `-`. `^` binds tighter than unary minus: `-2^2` is `-4`.

explanation.whatItIs: Numbers are values you do arithmetic with — health, coins, speed, positions, time. Luau doesn't force you to pick integer vs decimal up front: one number type handles both.
explanation.whyItExists: Everything measurable in a game is a number: damage, timers, probabilities, 3D coordinates.
whenNotToUse: Don't compare floats for exact equality after math — `0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3` is `false`. Use a tolerance for positions and timers
Don't use numbers where a string id is clearer (prefer tags/attributes over magic numbers)
tips: `math.clamp(value, min, max)` keeps a number in range — perfect for health bars
`math.random()` with no args gives a float in [0, 1); with one arg, integer 1..n; with two, integer m..n
String→number: `tonumber("42")` → 42 (nil if it can't parse); number→string: `tostring(42)`
commonMistakes: Integer division surprise: `7 / 2` is 3.5, not 3 — use `//` when you want 3
Floating point drift: adding 0.1 repeatedly never lands exactly on whole numbers
Forgetting `%` with negatives behaves toward +infinity semantics: `-7 % 3 == 2`

examples.title: Common number utilities in a game
examples.code:
local health = 100

local function takeDamage(amount)
    health = math.clamp(health - amount, 0, 100)
    print("Health:", health)
end

takeDamage(30)   --> Health: 70
takeDamage(999)  --> Health: 0   (clamped, never negative)

-- Random item from a loot table
local loot = {"Coin", "Gem", "Sword", "Nothing"}
local drop = loot[math.random(#loot)]
print("You got:", drop)
